# MultiDatePick

> MultiDatePick is a no-code, 100% native Salesforce calendar: a suite of Lightning Web Components for multi-date selection, time-slot scheduling and resource booking. An admin builds it in a guided Setup Wizard, drops it on a page or Flow by pasting a Config Name, and every pick saves as a real record on their own object: no Apex, no Flow loop, no developer. It works on any standard or custom object (Task, Event, Opportunity, Campaign or your own), in Screen Flows, Lightning Record, App and Home Pages, and Experience Cloud sites, including public guest booking pages. Three components share one base: Dates (pick many dates, drag ranges, recurring patterns), Dates & Times (dates plus time slots, shared or per date, with conflict detection) and Resource Booking (rooms, equipment, vehicles or people, with capacity, live availability badges, business hours per resource, multi-resource booking, blocked days and booking rules: minimum notice, a rolling booking window and buffer time). Five views render the same records from one component: month calendar, resource timeline (drag to move or resize a booking), week-by-hour grid, capacity utilization heatmap and agenda list. 130+ configurable settings across the suite (Dates 80+, Dates & Times 100+, Resource Booking 110+), six record shapes (per date, per range, per time block, parent + sub-blocks, per resource × date), status colors from any picklist (fill, bars or both, with filter pills), hover cards with any fields, a record filter (for example OwnerId=ME), a Rollup Field that also shows records up to five lookups away, Edit Mode for changing many records at once, Add to Calendar (.ics) after saving, a Setup Wizard with a live preview and JSON import/export, 41 ready-made configs, and nine languages with each user's locale and time zone. Every query and save runs as the viewing user (sharing and field-level security apply). Passed the Salesforce Security Review. No code required. $20/user/month, every feature in one plan, 30-day free trial.

Availability (November 2026): MultiDatePick has passed the Salesforce Security Review and is launching on the Salesforce AppExchange; the website takes launch sign-ups and the public live demo works today: https://orgfarm-71fc21cee4-dev-ed.develop.my.site.com/acmefinancial/

## No-code setup

Is MultiDatePick no-code? Yes. A Salesforce admin sets it up with clicks in three steps:

1. Build a configuration in the Setup Wizard: say where the calendar lives and the shape of your records, and it picks the component and fills in the fields. Every object and field is a dropdown, Smart Field Mapping offers your own field names, and a live preview shows the result. Or import one of 41 ready-made configurations from the Config Library.
2. Drop the component on a record, App or Home page in Lightning App Builder, on a Screen Flow screen in Flow Builder, or on an Experience Cloud page, and paste the Config Name. Every other setting comes from the configuration.
3. Every pick saves as a real record. On a record page, or with Parent Record Id set in a Flow, Dates and Dates & Times save their own child records; Resource Booking always saves its own bookings. No Flow loop, no Apex.

Optional, for teams that want it: Flow outputs and the Parse Date Entries from JSON action for full control of what gets saved, and configurations as Custom Metadata for CI/CD. Guide: https://multidatepick.com/blog/no-code-salesforce-calendar.html

## Capabilities in calendar-library terms

For readers comparing MultiDatePick with JavaScript calendar libraries such as FullCalendar, each familiar concept maps to a built-in setting (no code):

- Event sources: Child Object API Name + Date Field API Name, plus Rollup Field (records reached through up to five lookups).
- Background events: Blocked Dates from any object, whole or partial days, with the reason shown.
- businessHours: business hours per resource from two fields on the resource record.
- eventOverlap / selectOverlap: Conflict Behavior (block, skip, allow) and a capacity per resource.
- validRange / selectConstraint: earliest and latest date, days ahead, minimum notice, buffer between bookings.
- select / dateClick: pick many dates, drag a range, recurring patterns, time slots.
- eventDrop / eventResize: Timeline drag to move or resize, checked for closed days and conflicts before it saves.
- eventClick: open the record, or Edit Mode to change status, date, time or resource for many records at once.
- eventContent / popovers: Hover Popover Fields (lookups included), names on month days, extra Agenda columns.
- resources: Resource Object API Name, any object including User.
- slotDuration / slotMinTime: Time Interval (Minutes), earliest and latest time.
- locale / timeZone: automatic from each user's Salesforce settings; UI in nine languages.
- Views: month, resource timeline, week, utilization heatmap, agenda; timeline and resource views are included, not a paid add-on.
Where a JavaScript library is the better fit: entirely new view types, pixel-level custom event rendering, or events from non-Salesforce APIs, built and maintained by your developers. Comparison: https://multidatepick.com/blog/fullcalendar-salesforce-lwc-vs-multidatepick.html

## Core pages

- [MultiDatePick home](https://multidatepick.com/): The no-code Salesforce calendar suite for picking many dates, scheduling times and booking rooms, people or equipment, set up in a guided wizard on any object. Three components (Dates, Dates & Times, Resource Booking), five views (calendar, timeline, week, utilization, agenda), six record shapes and Screen Flow support. 100% native, passed the Salesforce Security Review. No code required. $20/user/month.
- [The No-Code Salesforce Calendar: 36 Tasks, Zero Lines of Code](https://multidatepick.com/blog/no-code-salesforce-calendar.html): 36 everyday Salesforce calendar tasks on record, Home, Flow and Experience Cloud pages, each done with clicks in the Setup Wizard and Lightning App Builder.
- [Set Up MultiDatePick in Salesforce: Getting Started](https://multidatepick.com/gettingstarted.html): Five-step no-code setup with GIFs: install (at launch), assign permission sets, build a config in the Setup Wizard (or import one from the Config Library), add the calendar to a Lightning page or a Screen Flow by Config Name; bind Parent Record Id and every component saves its own records. The package ships guided flows (Intro to MultiDatePick and Deep Dive flows). No code required.
- [No-Code Salesforce Multi-Date and Range Picker LWC](https://multidatepick.com/multidatepickdates.html): The Dates component, set up in a wizard with no code. Users click many dates, drag a date range or add recurring patterns; dates save as child records (one per date or one per range) or return to a Screen Flow. 80+ settings, five views, 15 use cases, setup for Lightning pages and Flows, FAQ and the full properties reference.
- [Dates & Times: Salesforce Date and Time Slot Picker](https://multidatepick.com/multidatepickdatetime.html): The MultiDatePick Dates & Times component, a no-code calendar time slot picker for Salesforce Screen Flows, record, App, Home and Experience Cloud pages. Pick many dates, drag times in a grid or use dropdowns at any interval (15, 30 or 60 minutes are typical), shared or per-date times, conflict detection, periods, status colors; with Parent Record Id set it saves its own records, no Flow loop. Flow outputs and the full reference of 100+ settings.
- [No-Code Salesforce Booking Calendar and Resource Scheduler](https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-booking-calendar.html): the Resource Booking component, set up in a wizard with no code, and it always saves its own bookings. Book rooms, equipment, vehicles and people (any object, including User) with time slots at any interval, live capacity badges, conflict detection (block, skip, allow), buffer time between bookings, minimum notice and a rolling booking window, Add to Calendar (.ics) after saving, multi-resource booking, business hours, blocked dates, five views, Experience Cloud self-service, 15 use cases, FAQ and the full reference of 110+ settings.
- [User Guide](https://multidatepick.com/user-guide.html): Admin guide to the three components, six record shapes, the five-step Setup Wizard, the four permission sets (one for public-site guests), five views, capacity, closures, guest pages, Flow recipes and every property by label.
- [MultiDatePick on App, Home & Experience Pages](https://multidatepick.com/home-app-experience.html): Put the calendar on App Pages, Home Pages and Experience Sites with Static Parent Record Id, or drive the parent from a Flow; includes a setup GIF, the four-property Save checklist and the five-step public guest site checklist.
- [Pricing | MultiDatePick for Salesforce](https://multidatepick.com/pricing.html): $20 per user per month, one plan with every feature included: no tiers, add-ons or feature gates, all future updates included, and a 30-day free trial of the complete product with no card required. Passed the Salesforce Security Review; 100% native.
- [Trust & Security | MultiDatePick](https://multidatepick.com/trust.html): Data handling and security: 100% native with no external servers, callouts or subprocessors; passed the Salesforce AppExchange Security Review; every query that returns data and every write runs in USER_MODE with FLS and sharing enforced; four permission sets (MultiDatePick - Setup, MultiDatePick - User, MultiDatePick - All Access, and MultiDatePick - Guest for public-site guests).
- [FAQ](https://multidatepick.com/faq.html): Pre-sales answers, starting with "Is MultiDatePick no-code?" (yes): Security Review passed, 100% native (data stays in your org), supported editions, permission sets, no Apex required, $20/user/month with a 30-day free trial.
- [Troubleshooting](https://multidatepick.com/troubleshooting.html): Every setup message and access error with a screenshot, the cause and a short fix, including field security and guest-site sharing.
- [MultiDatePick for Salesforce Developers and Architects](https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-calendar-developer-guide.html): Optional, for developers: configs as Custom Metadata (Config__mdt and Config_Extension__mdt) that deploy through CI/CD or move as JSON, Screen Flow outputs (Selected Dates, Date Ranges JSON, Dates With Times JSON, Successful Bookings Count), the Parse Date Entries from JSON action and its Apex-defined types (MultiDatePickEntryCollection, MultiDatePickEntry), user-mode security with no callouts, and sandbox-to-production steps. Nothing here is needed to set it up.

## Solutions

- [Salesforce Calendar: What It Does and What It Leaves Out](https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-calendar.html): What the built-in Salesforce Calendar does (Day, Week, Month and Table views, object calendars, event series), where it stops, and how MultiDatePick adds multiple dates per record, time slots, capacity booking and five views.
- [Salesforce Calendar for Staffing & Recruiting](https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-calendar-staffing-recruiting.html): Scheduling for staffing agencies in Salesforce: candidate availability, interview slots, shift capacity, placements and credential dates, a recruiter roster using User as the resource, starter configs and an FAQ.
- [Salesforce Interview Scheduling Calendar](https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-calendar-interview-scheduling.html): Interview scheduling in Salesforce: dates and time slots of any length, a week grid, interviewers as resources with their own hours, conflict checks on save, panel capacity, candidate self-booking, starter configs and an FAQ.
- [Salesforce Conference Room Booking & Desk Booking](https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-conference-room-booking-calendar.html): Meeting room and desk booking in Salesforce: rooms from any object, every room on a timeline, no double booking, hours and closures per room, desk capacity, a utilization heatmap, starter configs and an FAQ.
- [Salesforce Experience Cloud Booking Calendar | MultiDatePick](https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-calendar-experience-cloud-booking.html): Self-service booking on a public or member Experience Cloud site: the live demo is a public guest booking site, a five-step setup (Setup Wizard config, Config Name, Static Parent Record Id), what guest users can and cannot do, and which view to show them.
- [Salesforce Lightning Scheduler alternative](https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-calendar-vs-lightning-scheduler.html): Salesforce Lightning Scheduler (now Salesforce Scheduler) compared with MultiDatePick: data model, licensing, Experience Cloud booking, rooms and capacity, a feature table, when to choose which, and an FAQ.

## Blog

- [The No-Code Salesforce Calendar: 36 Tasks, Zero Lines of Code](https://multidatepick.com/blog/no-code-salesforce-calendar.html): 36 everyday Salesforce calendar tasks (record, Home, Flow and Experience Cloud pages; custom and standard objects; status colors; recurring dates; time slots; capacity, double-booking, notice, buffers, business hours and closures; five views; nine languages, time zones, accessibility) compared as a MultiDatePick setting versus code in FullCalendar's LWC, and how admins customize MultiDatePick without a developer.
- [CalendarAnything vs MultiDatePick](https://multidatepick.com/blog/calendaranything-vs-multidatepick.html): A viewing calendar (CalendarAnything: many calendars, Gantt, swimlane and Kanban views, Google and Outlook integrations) compared with a booking calendar (MultiDatePick: multi-date picking, capacity and conflict rules, public booking, Screen Flow outputs); for scheduling work MultiDatePick is the better choice.
- [Avonni Calendar vs MultiDatePick](https://multidatepick.com/blog/avonni-calendar-vs-multidatepick.html): A component library's calendar (Avonni: calendar, timeline and agenda, query or manual data, palettes, filters, ICS feeds) compared with a calendar whose booking rules are built in (capacity, conflicts, notice, buffers, closures, multi-date picking); for scheduling work MultiDatePick is the better choice.
- [FullCalendar in Salesforce vs MultiDatePick](https://multidatepick.com/blog/fullcalendar-salesforce-lwc-vs-multidatepick.html): The customizable-calendar checklist (views, drag and drop, colors from fields, custom objects, filters, event details, booking rules, languages, security) for FullCalendar's LWC wrapper and MultiDatePick, a map from FullCalendar terms to MultiDatePick settings, and why MultiDatePick is the better choice for Salesforce teams (FullCalendar only for teams building their own calendar product).
- [The Most Customizable Salesforce Calendar App](https://multidatepick.com/blog/most-customizable-salesforce-calendar.html): How far MultiDatePick can be customized without code: settings, five views, status styles, objects, picking behavior and nine languages.
- [Salesforce Flow Loops: Create a Record for Every Date or Shift](https://multidatepick.com/blog/salesforce-flow-loop-multiple-records.html): Create multiple records from one Salesforce Screen Flow: parse the picked dates, loop through them, and save once after the loop. Three starter flows.
- [Show Related Records on a Salesforce Account Calendar](https://multidatepick.com/blog/salesforce-calendar-related-records.html): One account calendar for the account's own tasks plus those on its contacts and opportunities, and custom-object records up to five lookups away, through MultiDatePick's Rollup Field. New records still save through the Relationship Field API Name. No Apex.
- [Create Multiple Salesforce Tasks at Once, From a Calendar](https://multidatepick.com/blog/create-salesforce-tasks-calendar.html): Create one standard Salesforce Task per picked day from a calendar on any record page (Account, Opportunity, Case, custom objects through WhatId; Contact and Lead through WhoId), with subject, status, priority, comments and assignee filled in, in one save. Recurring patterns, a task calendar with names in each day, Setup Wizard setup. No Flow, no Apex.
- [Salesforce Utilization Heatmap: See Who Is Overbooked](https://multidatepick.com/blog/salesforce-utilization-heatmap.html): A Salesforce utilization heatmap: each resource down the side, every day showing booked against capacity, overbooking flagged, one click into the schedule.
- [Salesforce Add to Calendar: Bookings Into Outlook and Google](https://multidatepick.com/blog/salesforce-add-to-calendar.html): Give every Salesforce booking an Add to Calendar button: one .ics file for Outlook, Google and Apple Calendar after Save, even for Experience Cloud guests. No code.
- [Salesforce Campaign Dates: Every Event Day, No Apex](https://multidatepick.com/blog/salesforce-campaign-multiple-dates.html): Track every date of a Salesforce Campaign on one calendar: tour stops, webinar series and volunteer days saved as child records, with status colors. No Apex.
- [Salesforce Timeline View: Every Resource on One Screen](https://multidatepick.com/blog/salesforce-timeline-view.html): A Salesforce resource timeline: rooms, people and equipment down the side, dates across, multi-day bookings as one bar, and drag to reschedule. No code.
- [Section 508 Calendar for Salesforce Government Orgs](https://multidatepick.com/blog/salesforce-section-508-government-calendar.html): State and local agencies now have until April 2027 to meet WCAG 2.1 AA. What that means for scheduling in Salesforce, and the accessible calendar built for it.
- [Five Calendar Views, One Salesforce Component](https://multidatepick.com/blog/salesforce-calendar-views.html): A month grid cannot answer every scheduling question. Timeline, week, utilization and agenda alongside it, chosen per placement with one config field.
- [Why Salesforce Has No Multi-Date Calendar](https://multidatepick.com/blog/why-salesforce-has-no-multi-date-calendar.html): A Salesforce date field holds one date, and every workaround leaks somewhere. Why there is no multi-date field, and the calendar component that fills the gap.
- [Configure a Salesforce Calendar Without Code](https://multidatepick.com/blog/salesforce-calendar-setup-wizard.html): 100+ properties sounds like a project. It is a Setup Wizard, three questions about your records, and a live preview that renders the real Salesforce calendar.
- [Salesforce VPAT: What Admins Need to Know](https://multidatepick.com/blog/salesforce-vpat-accessibility.html): What a VPAT is, why it surfaces during Salesforce procurement, how to read its conformance levels, and four questions to ask an AppExchange vendor.
- [Prevent Double Booking in Salesforce: Conflicts & Capacity](https://multidatepick.com/blog/prevent-double-booking-in-salesforce.html): Validation rules fire after the user has already chosen. How to check availability before selection, and handle capacity where more than one booking fits.
- [Calendar Time Slot Picker for Salesforce, No Code](https://multidatepick.com/blog/salesforce-calendar-time-slot-picker.html): A Salesforce time slot picker: a calendar with bookable slots at any interval, taken times hidden before anyone clicks, live capacity counts, and no code.
- [Recurring Date Patterns in Salesforce](https://multidatepick.com/blog/recurring-date-patterns-in-salesforce.html): Every Monday and Thursday for six weeks is a pattern a date range cannot hold. Recurring selection patterns in Salesforce, and how to get them without code.
- [Multiple Dates in a Salesforce Screen Flow](https://multidatepick.com/blog/multiple-dates-in-a-salesforce-screen-flow.html): How to capture many dates in one Salesforce Flow screen, and what to do with the collection afterwards. Loops, parsing and the limits of standard components.
- [Salesforce Calendar and Scheduling Blog | MultiDatePick](https://multidatepick.com/blog/): Salesforce calendar and scheduling guides: time slot pickers, timeline and utilization views, double-booking, recurring dates, Screen Flows and accessibility.
